subject: biology
title: Cell Division
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Cell Division — AQA GCSE Biology (8461) specification, section 4.1.2.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology (AQA) practice covering Cell Division, specification section 4.1.2.
final_note: You worked through Cell Division — 20 specification statements.

concepts.def: A structure found in the nucleus of a cell, made of a DNA molecule. Each chromosome carries a large number of genes.
A section of a DNA molecule carried on a chromosome. A single chromosome carries a large number of genes, so genes are much smaller structures than chromosomes.

concepts.term: Pairs of chromosomes in body cells
concepts.def: In body cells the chromosomes are normally found in pairs, so each type of chromosome is present twice in the nucleus.

The series of stages in which cells divide. During the cell cycle the genetic material is doubled and then divided into two identical cells. The three overall stages are growth with DNA replication, mitosis, and division of the cytoplasm and cell membranes.

concepts.term: Growth stage of the cell cycle
concepts.def: Before a cell can divide it needs to grow and increase the number of sub-cellular structures such as ribosomes and mitochondria. In this stage the DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome.
The stage of the cell cycle in which one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell and the nucleus divides.

concepts.term: Division of the cytoplasm and cell membranes
concepts.def: The final stage of the cell cycle, in which the cytoplasm and cell membranes divide to form two identical cells.
Cell division by mitosis is important in the growth and development of multicellular organisms, because it produces new cells that are identical to the parent cell.
An undifferentiated cell of an organism which is capable of giving rise to many more cells of the same type, and from which certain other cells can arise from differentiation.
Stem cells from human embryos, which can be cloned and made to differentiate into most different types of human cells.

concepts.term: Adult stem cells in bone marrow
concepts.def: Stem cells from adult bone marrow, which can form many types of cells including blood cells.
Tissue in plants that can differentiate into any type of plant cell, throughout the life of the plant.
A process in which an embryo is produced with the same genes as the patient. Stem cells from the embryo are not rejected by the patient's body so they may be used for medical treatment.

Stem cells from meristems in plants can be used to produce clones of plants quickly and economically. Rare species can be cloned to protect them from extinction, and crop plants with special features such as disease resistance can be cloned to produce large numbers of identical plants for farmers.

mcqs.q: Which statement about chromosomes and genes in a body cell is correct?
options: A gene is made of a large number of chromosomes.
Each chromosome carries one gene made of DNA.
Each chromosome in the nucleus is found singly.
Each chromosome carries a large number of genes.
mcqs.explain: The nucleus of a cell contains chromosomes made of DNA molecules, and each chromosome carries a large number of genes.

mcqs.q: How are the chromosomes normally arranged in a body cell?
options: Singly, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside the nucleus of the cell.
In pairs, inside a large gene in the cell.
In pairs, carrying a single gene per pair.
mcqs.explain: In body cells the chromosomes are normally found in pairs, and the chromosomes are contained in the nucleus of the cell.

mcqs.q: Which description gives the three overall stages of the cell cycle in the correct order?
options: The cell grows and copies its DNA, then the nucleus divides, then the cytoplasm divides.
The nucleus divides first, then the cell grows and copies its DNA, then the cytoplasm divides.
The cell grows and halves its DNA, then the nucleus divides, then the cytoplasm divides.
The cell grows and copies its DNA, then the nucleus divides, and division is complete.
mcqs.explain: Before a cell can divide it grows and the DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome; in mitosis one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell and the nucleus divides; finally the cytoplasm and cell membranes divide to form two identical cells.

mcqs.q: A human body cell containing 46 chromosomes divides by mitosis. What does each new cell contain?
options: 23 chromosomes, identical to the parent cell
46 chromosomes, different from the parent cell
46 chromosomes, identical to the parent cell
23 chromosomes, different from the parent cell
mcqs.explain: During the cell cycle the genetic material is doubled and then divided into two identical cells, so each new cell has the parent cell's 46 chromosomes.

mcqs.q: Before a cell divides it grows and increases its number of ribosomes and mitochondria. What happens to the DNA at this stage?
options: The DNA is halved to leave one copy of each chromosome.
The DNA replicates after the nucleus has divided in two.
The DNA is altered so the two new cells are different.
The DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome.
mcqs.explain: Before a cell can divide the DNA replicates to form two copies of each chromosome, which is how the genetic material is doubled.

mcqs.q: What happens during mitosis and the stage that follows it?
options: One set of chromosomes goes to each end, then the cytoplasm divides.
One set of chromosomes goes to each end, and the cell remains whole.
Half of each chromosome goes to each end, then the cytoplasm divides.
The chromosomes are shared unevenly, then the cytoplasm divides.
mcqs.explain: In mitosis one set of chromosomes is pulled to each end of the cell and the nucleus divides; finally the cytoplasm and cell membranes divide to form two identical cells.

mcqs.q: A cut on the arm of a fully grown adult heals as new skin cells are produced. Which statement about the new cells is correct?
options: New cells with half the chromosomes are made.
New identical cells are produced by mitosis.
New genetically different cells are produced.
Mitosis has stopped because the adult is grown.
mcqs.explain: Cell division by mitosis produces two identical cells and is important in the growth and development of multicellular organisms, which includes producing new skin cells in this context.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes a stem cell?
options: A specialised cell that carries out one particular function.
A bone marrow cell that forms most cell types in the body.
An undifferentiated cell that can give rise to other cells.
A plant cell taken from the meristem tissue of a plant.
mcqs.explain: A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell of an organism which is capable of giving rise to many more cells of the same type, and from which certain other cells can arise from differentiation.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the function of stem cells is correct?
options: Meristem tissue can differentiate into any type of plant cell.
Bone marrow stem cells can differentiate into any type of cell.
Embryonic stem cells are specialised for one particular job.
Meristem tissue stops making new cells as the plant matures.
mcqs.explain: Meristem tissue in plants can differentiate into any type of plant cell, throughout the life of the plant.

mcqs.q: Which statement about therapeutic cloning is correct?
options: The stem cells produced are rejected by the patient's body.
The stem cells are taken from the patient's bone marrow.
An embryo with the same genes as the patient is produced.
The cells produced are specialised for one particular job.
mcqs.explain: In therapeutic cloning an embryo is produced with the same genes as the patient, and stem cells from the embryo are not rejected by the patient's body so they may be used for medical treatment.

mcqs.q: Which statement about treatment with stem cells is correct?
options: It is a guaranteed cure for conditions such as paralysis.
It uses bone marrow stem cells to replace nerve cells.
It fails because the patient's body rejects the cells.
It may be able to help conditions such as paralysis.
mcqs.explain: Treatment with stem cells may be able to help conditions such as diabetes and paralysis.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the risks of using stem cells is correct?
options: Viral infection could be transferred to the patient.
The concerns are ethical rather than medical ones.
Cells from a cloned embryo are rejected by the body.
The cells cannot give rise to more cells of one type.
mcqs.explain: The use of stem cells has potential risks such as transfer of viral infection, and some people have ethical or religious objections.

mcqs.q: Why are stem cells from meristems used to clone rare plant species?
options: Different plants are produced quickly and economically.
Identical plants are produced quickly and economically.
Identical plants are produced slowly and at a high cost.
Identical plants are produced while the parent is young.
mcqs.explain: Stem cells from meristems in plants can be used to produce clones of plants quickly and economically, so rare species can be cloned to protect them from extinction.
